name: 快速 Shell
description: 给 Agent 的 POSIX 快速通道：内嵌 mvdan.cc/sh v3 的常驻守护进程，用 Go 原生实现了 29 个 Windows 上缺失的核心工具（ls/cat/cp/mv/rm/mkdir/touch/wc/head/tail/grep/sed/sort/uniq/find/stat/env/dirname/basename/tr/sleep/date/seq 等）。轻量命令的端到端开销从 PowerShell 7 的约 400ms 降到数十毫秒。对 PowerShell 专有语法（$env:、cmdlet、.ps1、反斜杠路径）和解析失败、命令缺失、工作目录无效的情况会明确返回 fallback，让模型立刻回退到内置 Bash 工具，保证语义不回退。单次输出上限 8MB，超出截断而不是卡死；默认工作目录与 Bash 一致（工作区根）。守护进程随插件启动、随插件退出，崩溃自动重启；不联网、不读项目文件、不碰凭据。

en.name: Fast Shell
en.description: A POSIX fast lane for the agent: a resident daemon embedding mvdan.cc/sh v3, with 29 coreutils implemented natively in Go for the ones Windows lacks (ls/cat/cp/mv/rm/mkdir/touch/wc/head/tail/grep/sed/sort/uniq/find/stat/env/dirname/basename/tr/sleep/date/seq and more). Lightweight commands cost about 1ms instead of the ~270ms a PowerShell 7 cold start takes. PowerShell-only syntax ($env:, cmdlets, .ps1, backslash paths), parse failures and missing commands return an explicit fallback so the model switches back to the built-in Bash tool and semantics never regress. The daemon starts with the plugin, stops with it, and restarts on crash. No network, no project file reads, no credentials.
en.safetyNotes: The plugin spawns only its own bundled binary (bin/fastsh.exe) and speaks a line-delimited JSON protocol over stdio. It never touches project files, the network, the clipboard or credentials. The registered tool takes a POSIX command string, an optional working directory and an optional timeout; the daemon runs the command in-process through the embedded shell interpreter with a hard timeout and an 8MB output cap. Commands that use PowerShell-only syntax, fail to parse as POSIX, or name a command unavailable in the POSIX environment are refused with fallback=true instead of being executed.

agentTools.name: fastsh_run
agentTools.description: Run a POSIX shell command through the embedded fast interpreter (mvdan.cc/sh v3) in a resident daemon. Use this instead of the Bash tool for lightweight commands: it costs tens of milliseconds end-to-end instead of the ~400ms a PowerShell cold start takes, and it ships 29 native coreutils (ls/cat/cp/mv/rm/mkdir/touch/wc/head/tail/grep/sed/sort/uniq/find/stat/env/dirname/basename/tr/sleep/date/seq). Write native POSIX syntax with forward-slash paths. Output up to 8MB is returned safely (larger output is truncated with a note, never hangs). It runs in the current workspace root by default, same as the Bash tool. If the result has fallback=true, do NOT retry here: call the Bash tool instead, because this command was refused as needing PowerShell semantics (reasons: pwsh_env_var, pwsh_cmdlet, pwsh_param, pwsh_operator, pwsh_script, pwsh_array, pwsh_block, win_backslash_path, win_relative_path, posix_parse_error, command_not_found, cwd_not_found, daemon_unavailable). Prefer this tool for read-only inspection (ls, cat, grep, find, wc, head, tail, stat, pwd) and simple pipelines; use the Bash tool for anything touching PowerShell, cmdlets, .ps1 scripts, Windows backslash paths, or long-running builds.

command.description: The POSIX command to run, e.g. 'ls -la' or 'cat package.json | head -20'. Use forward-slash paths and POSIX syntax.

cwd.description: Optional working directory. Defaults to the current workspace root.

timeoutMs.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (1-600000). Defaults to 60000.
